544959|2026-06.headline: Runwal Enterprises Q1 FY27 revenue fell to Rs 3,400 million (from Rs 4,462 million) on occupation-certificate-based recognition, while pre-sales rose ~5% to Rs 4,835 million.
544959|2026-06.overview: This was the maiden earnings call after the company's listing, with the IPO proceeds received in the first week of October 2026. Pre-sales rose about 5% YoY to Rs 4,835 million and collections rose to Rs 5,754 million from Rs 4,993 million. Revenue from operations declined to about Rs 3,400 million, which management attributed to revenue being recognised only on occupation certificate and possession. Management said debt has been cut to about Rs 1,900 million external debt post-IPO and debt-to-equity has fallen from about 3 to about 1.5, with fuller benefits visible from Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company issue stated guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna Kanodia said no specific guidance yet, but a general direction on growth (20-25% pre-sales) will be given while maintaining balance-sheet and margin health.

qa_highlights.question: Debt repayment plan and current debt level?
qa_highlights.answer: Pradumna said debt-to-equity fell from 3.1x to 1.5x and debt is now about Rs 1,900 crore external. Future borrowing will be limited and self-liquidating. Shashi Bhushan added that land monetisation to data operators is being considered, with JLL mandated and 10-12 interested parties.

qa_highlights.question: Where is the land for the data-centre monetisation and how much?

545004|2026-09.headline: Jio Platforms Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 11.4% YoY to ₹40,475 Cr, EBITDA up 16.6% to ₹21,879 Cr at a 54.1% margin.
545004|2026-09.overview: Q2 FY27 was the first quarter reported after listing; management reported 542.4 million customers, 36 million YoY net adds and 9.1 million adds in the quarter, with 5G base at 300 million. Consolidated revenue of ₹40,475 Cr grew 11.4% YoY, EBITDA of ₹21,879 Cr grew 16.6% and margin expanded about 250 bps YoY, with management saying ~78% of incremental revenue flowed to EBITDA. PAT rose 13.7% YoY to ₹8,387 Cr, and EBITDA less capex was ₹15,449 Cr for the quarter (up 52.5% YoY) and ₹32,130 Cr for H1. Management framed growth around four pillars (grow, deepen, convert, build) and pushed a 'digital gateway' model, while explicitly not using tariff hikes as the main ARPU lever. Net leverage was 0.11x at 30 September; the call also covered the IPO (about ₹30,188 Cr of issue proceeds, 24.5x oversubscribed) and international partnership plans.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said digital revenue will come from enterprise, home and mobility; partnership talks are two-way, with equal engagement on UBR and full OSS/BSS stack; no timing was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why there is no converged single bill for connectivity and digital services.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is focusing on converged go-to-market and one bill, but said that story is still to play out.

qa_highlights.answer: CFO said capex has peaked and will not exceed last year's level for four to five years; management said growth is the priority and dividends will be considered after the first listed year.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said tariffs depend on several factors and it will decide at the right time; ARPU rose 3.5% YoY organically, and the focus is digital services realisations.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said it will not give technology to domestic players, will avoid competing with partners, and the Radisys model is the reference for partnerships.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Gemini deal runs 18 months, is not near expiry, and that AI will be offered via the telecom harness to the full base; no token charging decided.

qa_highlights.answer: Management said satellite direct-to-device capacity is far lower than terrestrial (about 20 kbps per sq km), that Jio covers 99% of India's homes, and that it plans its own LEO system as a complement.

570004|2026-03.headline: Q4 FY26 revenue rose about 4% to INR1,800 crore and EBITDA about 7%, but a March raw-material shock cost an estimated INR200-250 crore of sales.
570004|2026-03.overview: Management said Q4 consolidated revenue was about INR1,800 crore versus about INR1,750 crore a year earlier, with Hi-Tech up about 8% and plastics down slightly. For FY26, revenue grew about 11% and Hi-Tech grew over 20%, while plastics grew only 2.4%. Reported PAT was negative at about INR40 crore due to one-time deferred tax unwinding, a Labour Code charge and non-cash NCD unwinding; management cited adjusted PAT of about INR133 crore. Management says debt repayments due in September and March FY27 are to be met from internal accruals and government receivables, with refinancing and equity as backups.

segments.commentary: Q4 revenue slightly down, EBITDA up 3.3%, margin 10.2% versus 9.7%. FY26 revenue grew only 2.4% and EBITDA declined. Overseas plastic sheet business is doing reasonably well.

590003|2026-09.headline: KVB Q2 FY27: net profit INR788 crores (+37% YoY), NIM held at 4.26%, credit cost 0.43%, and advances growth guided to 18-20% for FY27.
590003|2026-09.overview: Karur Vysya Bank reported a strong Q2 FY27 with net profit of INR788 crores, up 4% QoQ and 37% YoY, and operating profit of INR1,162 crores (+14% YoY, +6% QoQ). Total business reached INR2,39,712 crores (+5% QoQ, +18% YoY), with advances up 7% QoQ to INR1,11,589 crores and deposits up 5% QoQ to INR1,28,123 crores. Management guided to 18-20% credit growth, NIM of 4% plus, ROA of about 2% and GNPA below 1.5% for FY27, while flagging that funding costs and loan-yield competition may pressure margins in coming quarters. Management also said the write-off recovery contribution has fallen sharply, and that the bank will rely more on core earnings.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any stress in gold loans given rising gold loan NPAs seen in bureau data for some peers?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it has not seen stress on the ground. Retail gold is priced at about 14%, agri gold at 10.75%.

qa_highlights.question: How much bancassurance income is at risk from the proposed IRDA commission changes, and how will it be recouped?
qa_highlights.answer: Management estimated commissions could fall 60-70% in some cases. qa_highlights.question: How resilient are non-core income sources (treasury and write-off recoveries) to ROA?

qa_highlights.question: Is the corporate and SME demand driven by working capital drawdown or capex, and what is the textile utilisation?

qa_highlights.question: Why did RWA rise and what is driving the vehicle loan decline?

Vehicle loans are declining as a tactical call due to fixed rates, dealer commissions, high delinquency, 150% risk weight and deposit tightness; funds moved to gold and mortgages.

It expects 4%+ for the next 2 quarters, citing gold loan repricing from MCLR to fixed now complete, corporate yields of 9%+, and possible 3-6 month pricing pressure. EBLR book is about 56-57%, with working capital repricing 25 bps immediately.

590013|2026-03.headline: Xpro Q4 FY26 revenue fell to INR134.37 crore (vs INR158.2 crore) while PBT rose to INR16 crore; FY26 PBT fell to INR41 crore on forex loss and pre-operating costs.
590013|2026-03.overview: Q4 FY26 revenue from operations was INR134.37 crore against INR158.2 crore a year earlier, while quarterly PBT rose to INR16 crore from INR11.5 crore. Full-year net revenue fell 5.6% to INR505.5 crore and production fell 5% to 31,335 MT, driven by lower Coex (refrigerator sheet and liner) volumes. Full-year PBT fell to INR41 crore from INR58 crore, hit by competitive pricing, input cost volatility, a forex loss of INR11 crore (INR11.14 crore unrealised) and pre-operating costs. The new Barjora dielectric film line entered commercial production on 27 March 2026, and management said polymer prices are rising steeply after the West Asia crisis.

qa_highlights.question: What utilisation is expected on the new Barjora line?
qa_highlights.answer: Target of at least 50% during the year, 'if not more'; management declined to give a detailed marketing or production plan.

qa_highlights.question: When will the RAK (UAE) line start and what volumes are expected in FY27 and FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Trial production expected August-September 2026, commercial operations by Q3 FY27. Full utilisation of the two India lines expected next year, and UAE line above 50% in FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Biggest concerns for FY28 sales volumes: raw materials, pricing or new entrants?
qa_highlights.answer: New entrants are not a major concern; the main risks are West Asia-driven polymer supply and specialised grade availability, and forex volatility. Pricing is pass-through but price elasticity limits it.

qa_highlights.question: What share of Biax revenue could come from 2-3 micron films in 2-3 years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 2-3 micron as the modal mix is unrealistic near term; weighted average thickness is expected to move to about 4-5 micron within 2-3 years, with development efforts aimed higher than 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Raw material availability and visibility?
qa_highlights.answer: The company holds more than 3 months of imported raw material stock and is booking as material becomes available; European supply faces shipping cost and timing risk.

qa_highlights.question: What is the EBITDA margin expectation for the new line and Biax in FY27-FY28?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give margin figures and said only volume expectations were shared; EBITDA break-even on the second line was not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Price increase sustainability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said industrial pricing varies with polymer prices and exchange rates; it wants prices to stabilise at a decent level, with specialties keeping a premium.
